questions.explanation: Once a discrete GPU is installed, onboard video is often disabled, so the monitor must use the new card's ports.

questions.prompt: A phone charges only intermittently, even with a new cable and charger. What should the technician check NEXT?
questions.explanation: Lint packed into the charging port often blocks a solid connection; cleaning it is quick and non-invasive.

questions.prompt: A laptop's built-in screen is black, but an external monitor connected to it displays normally. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: A fault in the laptop's display hardware
questions.explanation: Because the GPU and OS work on the external display, the fault is in the laptop's own display hardware.

questions.prompt: After a drop, a tablet ignores touch in one area even though the image displays normally. What part MOST likely needs replacement?
questions.explanation: The digitizer handles touch input, so a dead touch zone with a normal image points to it.

questions.prompt: A user dropped a phone into water and it still appears to work. What should be advised FIRST?
choices: Charge it fully to test the battery
Place it in a hot oven to dry
Power it off and do not charge it
questions.explanation: Powering off and not charging reduces the risk of short circuits while the device dries or is serviced.

questions.prompt: A laser printer prints faint duplicate images of earlier content lower on each page. Which component is MOST likely at fault?
questions.explanation: Ghost images usually come from an imaging drum that is not being fully cleaned or discharged between rotations.

questions.prompt: A printer in a humid storage room keeps jamming, and pages come out wrinkled. What is the BEST fix?
questions.explanation: Damp paper curls and sticks together, causing jams and wrinkles; it should be stored in a dry place.

questions.prompt: A printer outputs pages of random symbols and garbled characters. What is the MOST likely cause?
questions.explanation: Garbled output means the printer is getting data it cannot interpret, typically from a wrong or corrupt driver.

questions.prompt: After an office network change, users can no longer print to a network printer whose IP address changed. What is the BEST long-term fix?
choices: Switch all users to USB printing
Reinstall the operating system on each PC
Reserve the printer's IP and update the port
questions.explanation: A DHCP reservation keeps the printer's address fixed, and updating the printer port points PCs to it.

questions.prompt: A user can ping 127.0.0.1 but not the default gateway. What does this indicate?
choices: The remote website is currently down
The DNS server for the office is offline
The TCP/IP stack on the PC is corrupted
The local stack works, but the link or config is faulty
questions.explanation: A successful loopback ping proves the local stack is fine, so the fault lies in the cable, NIC, switch or configuration.

questions.prompt: A PC can reach shares on the local network but not the internet. ipconfig shows no default gateway. What should be done?
questions.explanation: Without a default gateway, traffic cannot leave the local subnet to reach the internet.

questions.prompt: A laptop's Wi-Fi drops whenever the break room microwave is running. What is the BEST fix?
choices: Connect the laptop to the 5 GHz band
Move the laptop closer to the microwave
questions.explanation: Microwave ovens interfere with 2.4 GHz; the 5 GHz band avoids that interference.

questions.prompt: A cable tester shows one pair as open on a newly installed run. What should the technician do?
questions.explanation: An open pair means a broken or poorly seated wire, usually fixed by re-terminating the connector.

questions.prompt: A PC connected with a 130-meter Cat 6 run has frequent errors and slow throughput. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: An incorrect subnet mask on the PC
questions.explanation: Copper Ethernet runs are limited to 100 meters; longer runs suffer signal loss and errors.

questions.prompt: One drive in a two-drive RAID 0 array has failed. What is the outcome?
choices: The remaining drive keeps a full mirrored copy
The array runs in degraded mode until rebuilt
Parity data rebuilds the failed drive automatically
The array is lost and data must be restored from backup
questions.explanation: RAID 0 has no redundancy, so losing any one drive destroys the whole array.

questions.prompt: A newly added second drive does not appear in File Explorer, but Disk Management shows it as unallocated. What should be done?
choices: Initialize the disk and create a volume
Run the System File Checker tool
questions.explanation: A new drive must be initialized, partitioned and formatted before Windows assigns it a drive letter.

questions.prompt: After reinstalling a CPU cooler, a PC shuts off a few minutes after boot. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: The cooler is poorly seated or lacks paste
The RAM is running in single-channel mode
The hard drive has bad sectors
questions.explanation: Poor cooler contact causes the CPU to overheat quickly, triggering thermal shutdown.

questions.prompt: An office PC is running loud and slow, and monitoring software shows high CPU temperatures. The vents are clogged. What should the technician do?
choices: Blow out the dust with compressed air
questions.explanation: Dust blocks airflow, causing overheating and throttling; cleaning restores cooling.

questions.prompt: Which Windows command lists active TCP connections and the ports the computer is listening on?
questions.explanation: netstat shows active connections and listening ports; adding -b shows which program owns each one.

questions.prompt: Which Windows command displays only the computer's name?
questions.explanation: hostname prints the computer name; whoami shows the logged-in user account.

questions.prompt: Which command restarts a Windows PC immediately with no delay?
questions.explanation: shutdown /r restarts the PC, and /t 0 sets the delay to zero seconds.

questions.prompt: A technician needs to quickly confirm which Windows version and build a PC is running. Which command opens that information?
questions.explanation: winver opens the About Windows dialog showing the edition, version and build number.

questions.prompt: A technician wants a PC to start in Safe Mode on its next restart from within Windows. Which tool provides a Safe boot option?
questions.explanation: The Boot tab in msconfig has a Safe boot checkbox that applies on the next restart.

questions.prompt: Which Windows tool lets a technician directly view and edit the hierarchical database of system and application settings?
questions.explanation: regedit edits the Windows Registry; changes should be made carefully and backed up first.

questions.prompt: A newly updated network driver causes connection drops. Where can the technician revert to the previous driver?
questions.explanation: Device Manager's Roll Back Driver option on the driver tab restores the previously installed driver.

questions.prompt: A technician needs to extend a Windows data volume into adjacent unallocated space using a graphical tool. Which tool should be used?
questions.explanation: Disk Management can create, extend, shrink and format volumes and assign drive letters.

questions.prompt: A technician wants to log CPU and disk counters over several days to find a performance pattern. Which tool is BEST?
questions.explanation: Performance Monitor can collect counter data over time with data collector sets; Task Manager shows only live data.

questions.prompt: Which Windows tool gives a detailed inventory of hardware resources, components and the software environment?
questions.explanation: msinfo32 summarizes hardware, IRQs, components and drivers in one report.

questions.prompt: A user has graphics and sound problems in a game. Which Windows tool reports DirectX, display and audio driver details?
questions.explanation: The DirectX Diagnostic Tool lists display and sound devices, drivers and DirectX features.

questions.prompt: A technician needs to view and import a user's personal digital certificates in Windows. Which console should be opened?
questions.explanation: certmgr.msc manages the current user's certificate store.

questions.prompt: On a standalone Windows Pro PC, which tool sets local policies such as password rules and software restrictions?
questions.explanation: gpedit.msc edits local policies on Pro and higher editions; Home editions do not include it.

questions.prompt: A user's PC is low on space from temporary files and the Recycle Bin. Which built-in tool safely removes these?
questions.explanation: Disk Cleanup (cleanmgr) deletes temporary files, cached update files and the Recycle Bin contents.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum RAM required to install Windows 11?
questions.explanation: Windows 11 requires at least 4 GB of RAM and 64 GB of storage, along with TPM 2.0 and UEFI Secure Boot support.

questions.prompt: A PC has 16 GB of RAM installed, but Windows shows less than 4 GB usable. What is the MOST likely reason?
choices: A 32-bit version of Windows is installed
The RAM is running in dual-channel mode
questions.explanation: A 32-bit OS can address only about 4 GB of memory; a 64-bit OS is needed to use more.

questions.prompt: A technician is partitioning a new 4 TB drive and wants to use all of its space. Why is MBR a poor choice?
choices: MBR supports disks only up to 2 TB
MBR requires UEFI firmware to boot
MBR does not work with NTFS
questions.explanation: MBR is limited to 2 TB and four primary partitions; GPT supports far larger disks.

questions.prompt: A user wants to reinstall Windows on a sluggish PC while keeping personal files. Which built-in option fits BEST?
choices: Reset this PC with Keep my files
Format the drive and clean install
questions.explanation: Reset this PC reinstalls Windows and can keep personal files while removing apps and settings.

questions.prompt: A five-person office with no server wants to share files between Windows PCs. Which network model should be used?
questions.explanation: A workgroup is a peer-to-peer model where each PC manages its own accounts, suitable for small offices with no server.

questions.prompt: Which hidden administrative share gives administrators remote access to the root of a Windows PC's system drive?
questions.explanation: Windows automatically creates hidden admin shares like C$ for the root of each drive.

questions.prompt: A user connects a Windows laptop to a phone hotspot and wants to limit background downloads. Which setting should be enabled?
questions.explanation: Marking a network as metered reduces background data use such as some updates and syncing.

questions.prompt: Which macOS feature shows all open windows and lets the user create additional virtual desktops called Spaces?
questions.explanation: Mission Control displays open windows and manages multiple desktops (Spaces).

questions.prompt: Which keyboard shortcut opens the Force Quit Applications window on macOS?
questions.explanation: Command+Option+Escape opens Force Quit, similar to ending a task in Windows Task Manager.

questions.prompt: A Mac user downloaded an app as a disk image they must open and drag to Applications. Which file extension is it?
questions.explanation: macOS apps are often distributed as .dmg disk images; .msi and .exe are Windows installers.

questions.prompt: Which command displays IP addresses for network interfaces on a modern Linux system?
questions.explanation: ip addr (part of the ip utility) shows interface addresses on Linux; ipconfig is the Windows equivalent.

questions.prompt: A Linux user wants to read the built-in documentation for the chmod command. Which command should be used?
questions.explanation: The man command opens the manual page for a Linux command.

questions.prompt: Which Linux command is used to rename a file?
questions.explanation: mv moves or renames files; cp copies them and leaves the original in place.

questions.prompt: A technician needs to edit a configuration file from a Linux terminal with a simple text editor. Which command should be used?
questions.explanation: nano is a simple terminal text editor; grep searches text and df reports disk space.

questions.prompt: Which WPA3 feature replaces the pre-shared key handshake to resist offline dictionary attacks?
questions.explanation: Simultaneous Authentication of Equals (SAE) protects against offline password guessing better than WPA2-PSK.

questions.prompt: Which encryption method does WPA2 use for strong wireless security?
questions.explanation: WPA2 uses AES with CCMP; TKIP is older and weaker.

questions.prompt: Which authentication protocol do Windows domains use by default, issuing tickets from the domain controller?
questions.explanation: Active Directory uses Kerberos, which issues time-limited tickets to authenticate users and services.

questions.prompt: Which AAA protocol, common for network device administration, uses TCP and separates authentication, authorization and accounting?
questions.explanation: TACACS+ uses TCP and handles each AAA function separately; RADIUS uses UDP and combines authentication and authorization.

questions.prompt: Which type of malware secretly monitors a user's activity and sends information such as browsing habits to a third party?
questions.explanation: Spyware collects data about the user without consent and sends it to the attacker.

questions.prompt: Which type of malware records each key a user presses to capture passwords?
questions.explanation: A keylogger captures keystrokes, often to steal credentials; it can be software or a hardware device.

questions.prompt: Thousands of infected home PCs are controlled remotely by an attacker to send spam. What are these PCs part of?
questions.explanation: A botnet is a network of compromised computers controlled by an attacker through command-and-control servers.

questions.prompt: A PC's CPU runs at 100% all day due to hidden software using its resources to generate digital currency for an attacker. What type of malware is this?
questions.explanation: Cryptominers hijack computing power to mine cryptocurrency, causing high resource usage.

questions.prompt: A phishing email is crafted specifically to target a company's CFO. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Whaling is spear phishing aimed at high-level executives.

questions.prompt: An attacker searches through a company's trash to find printed passwords and network diagrams. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Dumpster diving recovers sensitive information from discarded materials, which is why shredding policies matter.

questions.prompt: A website is overwhelmed by traffic from thousands of compromised devices at once. What type of attack is this?
questions.explanation: A distributed denial-of-service attack uses many sources to flood a target and make it unavailable.

questions.prompt: An attacker injects malicious script into a website comment field so it runs in other visitors' browsers. What attack is this?
questions.explanation: XSS injects client-side scripts into web pages viewed by other users; SQL injection targets the database.

questions.prompt: A receptionist's monitor faces the lobby and visitors can read the screen. Which control BEST reduces this risk?
questions.explanation: A privacy filter narrows the viewing angle so only the person in front of the screen can read it.

questions.prompt: Which physical control uses short, sturdy posts to stop vehicles from driving into a building entrance?
questions.explanation: Bollards are barriers that block vehicles while allowing pedestrians through.

questions.prompt: Laptops in a public computer lab are being stolen from desks. Which control is the BEST low-cost fix?
questions.explanation: Cable locks physically attach laptops to furniture; encryption protects data but does not prevent theft.

questions.prompt: A company wants to stop malware from launching automatically when USB drives are inserted. Which setting should be disabled?
questions.explanation: Disabling AutoRun and AutoPlay prevents removable media from running code automatically when connected.

questions.prompt: Which Windows feature encrypts removable USB flash drives?
questions.explanation: BitLocker To Go extends BitLocker encryption to removable drives.

questions.prompt: A user wants to encrypt a single folder on an NTFS drive so it can be read only by their own account. Which feature should be used?
questions.explanation: The Encrypting File System encrypts individual files and folders tied to the user's account; BitLocker encrypts whole volumes.

questions.prompt: A laptop joins a coffee shop's Wi-Fi network. Which Windows Defender Firewall profile should be applied for the strictest settings?
questions.explanation: The Public profile is the most restrictive and should be used on untrusted networks.

questions.prompt: Users often leave their desks with their PCs unlocked. Which control BEST addresses this?
choices: An automatic screen lock after inactivity
questions.explanation: An inactivity timeout locks the screen automatically when a user forgets to.

questions.prompt: A company wants a lost phone's data protected if someone repeatedly guesses the passcode. Which policy should be configured?
choices: Wipe the device after repeated failed unlocks
Allow only cellular data on the device
questions.explanation: A failed-attempt limit that triggers a wipe stops brute-force guessing of the passcode.

questions.prompt: Which SOHO router feature should be disabled because its PIN method can be brute-forced?
questions.explanation: Wi-Fi Protected Setup's PIN method is vulnerable to brute-force attacks, so it should be turned off.

questions.prompt: Which ongoing task BEST protects a SOHO router against newly discovered vulnerabilities?
questions.explanation: Firmware updates patch security flaws in the router's software.

questions.prompt: Which SOHO router control lets only devices with specific hardware addresses join the network, though it can be spoofed?
questions.explanation: MAC filtering allows or denies devices by MAC address, but attackers can spoof allowed addresses.

questions.prompt: A technician downloads a browser installer and wants to confirm it was not tampered with. What should be done?
choices: Rename the file before running it
Run the installer in compatibility mode
Check that the file name matches the vendor
Compare its hash with the vendor's published hash
questions.explanation: A matching hash value confirms the file's integrity against what the vendor published.

questions.prompt: A user on a shared library computer does not want browsing history or cookies kept after the session. Which feature should be used?
questions.explanation: Private or incognito mode discards history, cookies and form data when the window closes.

questions.prompt: Employees reuse the same weak password on many websites. Which tool BEST helps them use unique strong passwords?
questions.explanation: Password managers generate and securely store unique complex passwords for each site.

questions.prompt: An attacker tries thousands of common words and leaked passwords from a list against a login. What type of attack is this?
questions.explanation: A dictionary attack uses a word list of likely passwords instead of trying every possible combination.

questions.prompt: A Windows service fails to start, and the error says a dependency service failed to start. What should the technician check?
choices: The amount of free disk space
questions.explanation: A service will not start if a required dependency is stopped or disabled; the Dependencies tab lists them.

questions.prompt: A USB scanner shows as an unknown device with a yellow warning in Device Manager. What should be done?
choices: Install or update the device driver
Run Disk Cleanup to free space
Change the power plan to High performance
questions.explanation: A yellow warning indicates a driver problem, so installing the correct driver usually fixes it.

questions.prompt: A PC with a mechanical drive has become very slow, and the drive is 98% full. What should be done FIRST?
questions.explanation: Nearly full drives leave little room for the page file and temporary files; freeing space is the first, least invasive step.

questions.prompt: A user with two monitors must move the mouse off the right edge of one screen to reach the other, which sits on the left. How should this be fixed?
choices: Swap the video cables between GPUs
questions.explanation: Display settings let you drag the monitor icons to match their physical layout.

questions.prompt: According to CompTIA's malware removal procedure, what should be done right after investigating and verifying the malware symptoms?
questions.explanation: After verifying symptoms, the infected system is quarantined to stop the spread before further steps.

questions.prompt: What is the LAST step in CompTIA's malware removal procedure?
choices: Enable System Restore and create a restore point
questions.explanation: After re-enabling System Restore and creating a restore point, the final step is user education to prevent reinfection.

questions.prompt: A pop-up claiming to be antivirus software reports dozens of infections and demands payment to clean them. What is this MOST likely?
questions.explanation: Fake antivirus pop-ups use scare tactics to trick users into paying or installing more malware.

questions.prompt: A PC goes to a fake site when a user types a bank's correct web address, but other PCs reach it fine. Which file should be checked for malicious entries?
questions.explanation: Malware can add entries to the hosts file to redirect specific domains to attacker-controlled IP addresses.

questions.prompt: A user's contacts report receiving spam that appears to come from the user's email account. What is the BEST first step?
choices: Reset the password and enable MFA
questions.explanation: Spam sent from the account indicates it is compromised; resetting credentials and adding MFA stops further misuse.

questions.prompt: A phone has become sluggish and apps open slowly, and settings show storage almost full. What should be done FIRST?
questions.explanation: Low storage slows mobile devices; clearing space is quick and non-destructive.

questions.prompt: A phone no longer connects to a Bluetooth car stereo it used to pair with. What should be tried FIRST?
choices: Remove the pairing and pair again
questions.explanation: Removing and re-creating the pairing clears corrupted pairing data.

questions.prompt: An app loads data on Wi-Fi but shows 'no connection' on cellular, while other apps work on cellular. What is the MOST likely cause?
choices: Cellular data is off for that app
The phone's SIM card is damaged
The app needs a factory reset
questions.explanation: Phones let users block cellular data per app; since other apps work, that setting is the likely cause.

questions.prompt: An MDM console flags an employee's phone because its built-in OS restrictions have been removed to allow unauthorized software. What has happened?
choices: The device is in airplane mode
questions.explanation: Rooting or jailbreaking bypasses OS security controls, so MDM policies often block such devices.

questions.prompt: An Android phone began showing ads everywhere after the user installed an app downloaded from a website instead of the app store. What is the MOST likely cause?
questions.explanation: Installing APKs from unknown sources bypasses store vetting and is a common route for adware and malware.

questions.prompt: A user installs a free flashlight app that requests access to contacts, microphone and location. What should the technician advise?
choices: Restart the phone to reset permissions
Turn on airplane mode while using it
Uninstall the app due to its excessive permissions
Grant the permissions so the light works
questions.explanation: A flashlight does not need contacts or location; excessive permission requests are a warning sign of data-harvesting apps.

questions.prompt: An older business application fails to run correctly on Windows 11 but worked on an older version. What should be tried FIRST?
questions.explanation: Compatibility mode emulates an earlier Windows version and can let older apps run on newer systems.

questions.prompt: Domain users on one PC get login errors, and the PC's clock is 20 minutes off from the domain controller. What should be done?
choices: Rejoin the PC to a workgroup
Sync the PC's clock with the domain
questions.explanation: Kerberos requires clocks to be closely synchronized; large time differences cause authentication failures.

questions.prompt: A user complains that Windows restarts to install updates while they are working during the day. What should be configured?
questions.explanation: Active hours tell Windows when the user is usually working so it avoids automatic restarts then.

questions.prompt: Malware keeps returning after every removal attempt while Windows is running normally. What should the technician try?
choices: Increase the size of the page file
Scan from Safe Mode or a boot environment
questions.explanation: Running scans outside the normal OS stops the malware from loading and protecting itself.

questions.prompt: After logging in, a Windows user sees only a black screen with a mouse cursor. What can the technician try FIRST?
questions.explanation: A black screen with a cursor often means Explorer failed to load; starting explorer.exe from Task Manager restores the desktop.

questions.prompt: A phone no longer connects to the home Wi-Fi after the router's password was changed. What should be done?
choices: Reset all phone settings to factory
Forget the network and rejoin it
questions.explanation: The phone keeps trying the saved old password; forgetting the network lets the user enter the new one.

questions.prompt: Windows shows 'Your system is low on virtual memory' even though plenty of disk space exists. What should be checked?
choices: Whether the paging file is disabled or too small
Whether the monitor's refresh rate is correct
questions.explanation: Virtual memory depends on the paging file; if it is disabled or capped too low, Windows reports low virtual memory.

questions.prompt: A user says their phone has stopped ringing for calls, though calls appear as missed. What should be checked FIRST?
choices: Whether the SIM card is damaged
Whether Do Not Disturb is enabled
questions.explanation: Do Not Disturb or focus modes silence incoming calls while still logging them as missed.

questions.prompt: Which ticket field ranks how urgently an issue must be handled based on its business impact?
questions.explanation: Priority, based on impact and urgency, determines response order and SLA timing.

questions.prompt: A company wants to track who has each laptop and when its warranty expires. What should be used?
choices: Asset tags and an inventory system
questions.explanation: Asset tags linked to an inventory database record ownership, location and warranty details.

questions.prompt: A technician solves a tricky printer issue and wants others to fix it faster next time. What should be created?
questions.explanation: Knowledge base articles document solutions so other technicians can reuse them.

questions.prompt: In change management, which group reviews and approves or rejects proposed changes?
questions.explanation: The change advisory board (CAB) evaluates risk and impact before approving a change.

questions.prompt: Before rolling out a major software update to all users, what should be done to reduce risk?
choices: Install it only on executives' PCs
Deploy it to everyone at once
Test it in a sandbox environment first
questions.explanation: Testing in an isolated environment finds problems before they affect production users.

questions.prompt: Which backup type combines an earlier full backup with later incremental backups to build a new full backup without reading the source again?
questions.explanation: A synthetic full is assembled from existing backup data, reducing load on the production system.

questions.prompt: An office runs nightly backups but has never tried restoring from them. What is the BEST recommendation?
questions.explanation: Only test restores prove that backups are complete and recoverable.

questions.prompt: Which backup rotation scheme uses daily, weekly and monthly backup sets?
questions.explanation: In GFS, son backups are daily, father backups are weekly and grandfather backups are monthly.

questions.prompt: A power supply has failed in a desktop. What is the SAFEST approach?
choices: Use an ESD strap while repairing the inside
Open it while it is plugged in to test
Replace the whole unit rather than opening it
Open it and replace the capacitors
questions.explanation: PSUs hold dangerous charges in their capacitors even when unplugged, so they are replaced, not repaired.

questions.prompt: Which class of fire extinguisher is used for electrical fires in the United States?
questions.explanation: Class C extinguishers, such as CO2, are rated for energized electrical equipment; Class A is for ordinary combustibles.

questions.prompt: Why is very low humidity a concern in a room full of computer equipment?
choices: It causes condensation on circuit boards
It increases the risk of static discharge
It raises the risk of corrosion
questions.explanation: Dry air allows static charge to build up, raising ESD risk; high humidity causes condensation.

questions.prompt: How should an empty laser printer toner cartridge be disposed of?
choices: Burn it to destroy the toner
Throw it in the regular office trash
Recycle it according to local regulations
Empty the residue into a sink
questions.explanation: Toner cartridges should be recycled or returned per local regulations and the SDS guidance.

questions.prompt: Which device protects equipment from voltage spikes but does not provide power during an outage?
questions.explanation: A surge suppressor blocks spikes; a UPS adds battery power for outages.

questions.prompt: Which document is the legal agreement that sets how a user may use a piece of software?
questions.explanation: The end-user license agreement defines software usage rights and restrictions.

questions.prompt: Which regulation governs how organizations handle the personal data of people in the European Union?
questions.explanation: The General Data Protection Regulation sets rules for collecting and processing EU residents' personal data.

questions.prompt: A technician is explaining a repair to a non-technical customer. What is the BEST approach?
choices: Use technical terms to show expertise
Use plain language and avoid jargon
questions.explanation: Clear, non-technical language helps customers understand and builds trust.

questions.prompt: A repair will take longer than expected because a part is on backorder. What should the technician do?
choices: Install a used part without asking
Close the ticket and reopen it later
Inform the customer and give a new timeline
Wait until the part arrives to say anything
questions.explanation: Setting and updating expectations keeps the customer informed and avoids frustration.

questions.prompt: Which file extension is used for Windows batch scripts?
questions.explanation: .bat files run commands in the Windows command interpreter; .sh is for Unix shells and .ps1 for PowerShell.

questions.prompt: A managed service provider wants to monitor client PCs, push patches and run scripts remotely from one console. Which tool fits BEST?
questions.explanation: RMM platforms combine monitoring, patching, scripting and remote control for many endpoints.

questions.prompt: An employee wants to paste customer records into a public AI chatbot to summarize them. What is the MAIN concern?
choices: Sensitive data may be exposed to others
The chatbot cannot read text input
The chatbot will slow down the network
The summary will be too short to use
questions.explanation: Public AI tools may store or use submitted data, so company policy should prohibit entering sensitive information.

questions.prompt: An AI assistant gives a confident answer that includes a command that does not exist. What is this called?
questions.explanation: AI hallucinations are plausible-sounding but incorrect outputs, so AI answers should be verified before use.
